([[Torrelodones]], Spain) | college = * [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]] (2020–2023) * [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 57 | draft_team = [[Orlando Magic]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[Maine Celtics]] | years3 = 2026–present | team3 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | highlights = * [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 Player of the Year]] (2025) * 2× First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2024, 2025) }} '''Maksym Shulga''' ({{langx|uk|Максим Шульга}}; born June 25, 2002) is a Ukrainian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State Aggies]] and the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]]. In the [[2025 NBA draft]], he was selected with the 57th overall pick by the [[Orlando Magic]], and traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), where he played eleven games. ==Early life and education== Shulga was born and grew up in [[Kyiv]], Ukraine.{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/basketball/vcu/men/article_acc65902-f653-11ef-9c90-9b8357ce80ee.html|title=VCU fans plan 'moment for Max,' will fly Ukrainian flags at Shulga's last home game|first=Zach|last=Joachim|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=March 3, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2025}} He moved to Spain at age 11 to study and play basketball in Colegio Leones in [[León, Spain|León]]. At age 14 he moved to [[Madrid]] to attend the Basketball School of Excellence in [[Torrelodones]].{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/sean-bairstow-max-shulga-vcu-basketball-ryan-odom-utah-state-rams/article_58b784a8-2fc1-11ee-8b3d-fb66a118a41f.html|title=VCU basketball transfers Bairstow, Shulga share close bond|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=August 3, 2023|access-date=March 5, 2025}} Shulga committed to play college basketball in the United States at [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/5/20/21265294/utah-state-university-aggies-mens-basketball-commit-ukrainian-national-max-shulga/|title=Utah State men's basketball adds another commit in Ukrainian national Max Shulga|first=Trent|last=Wood|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=May 20, 2020|access-date=March 3, 2025}} ==College career== ===Utah State=== Shulga began his college career at [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-state-sports/2022/03/01/he-prepares-his-next-game/|title=Utah State's Max Shulga's thoughts are with his family in Ukraine as he prepares for Aggies' next game|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=March 1, 2022|access-date=March 5, 2025}} He was named honorable mention All-[[Mountain West Conference]] as a junior after averaging 11.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, and four assists per game. After the season and the departure of Aggies' head coach [[Ryan Odom]], he entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-state-sports/2023/04/03/2-utah-state-basketball-starters/|title=2 Utah State basketball starters enter transfer portal|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=March 1, 2025}} ===VCU=== Shulga transferred to [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], following Odom.{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcu-hoops-lands-utah-state-transfers-sean-bairstow-max-shulga/article_23359244-e240-11ed-9bbd-b3d1894db7a9.html|title=VCU basketball lands Utah State transfers Shulga, Bairstow|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=April 23, 2023|access-date=March 5, 2025}} He was named first-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] in his first season with the Rams after averaging 14 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/villanova-basketball-max-shulga-commit-transfer-portal-20240503.html|title=VCU transfer Max Shulga gives Villanova playmaking and shooting as its roster continues to take shape|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=May 3, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2025}} Shulga re-entered the transfer portal at the end of the season and initially committed to transfer to [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], but ultimately decommitted and returned to VCU.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/max-shulga-decomits-villanova-vcu-20240522.html|title=Max Shulga withdraws his commitment to Villanova and plans to return to VCU|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=May 22, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2025}} In his final year at VCU, Shulga averaged a career-high 15 points, 5.9 rebounds, and four assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/max-shulga-1.html|title=Max Shulga|date=March 21, 2025|access-date=May 21, 2025|publisher=sports-reference.com}} Shulga led the Rams to both the Atlantic 10 Conference regular season and [[Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|Atlantic 10 tournament]] championships, winning the [[2025 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|2025 A-10 tournament title]] and the conference's automatic bid to the NCAA tournament. They won 18 of their final 20 games en route to a No. 11 seed in the NCAA tournament, where they lost to No. 6 seed [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] in the first round.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44343773/vcu-ryan-odom-emerges-top-virginia-candidate|title=VCU's Ryan Odom hired as Virginia men's basketball coach|date=March 21, 2025|accessdate=March 22, 2025|first1=Pete|last1=Thamel|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|publisher=espn.com}} ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2025–2026)=== Shulga was one of 75 players invited to the 2025 [[NBA draft combine]] in May 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-draft-combine-list-of-invites|title=NBA announces 75 players invited to participate at 2025 NBA Draft Combine|date=May 2, 2025|access-date=May 21, 2025|publisher=nba.com}} He was selected with the 57th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite web |title=VCU's Max Shulga selected in 2nd round of NBA Draft by Orlando Magic, traded to Boston Celtics |url=https://www.wtvr.com/sports/max-shulga-drafted-orlando-magic-june-26-2025 |website=WTVR.com |access-date=June 29, 2025 |date=June 26, 2025}} and his rights were then traded to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |last1=Snow |first1=Taylor |title=Celtics Trade Back in 2nd Round of Draft, Acquire Williams, Shulga & Future Picks |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar-offseason-20250626-celtics-trade-back-in-2nd-round-of-draft-acquiring-williams-shulga-amp-future-picks |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 29, 2025 |date=June 27, 2025}} On August 7, 2025, Boston signed Shulga to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Max Shulga to Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/celtics-sign-max-shulga-to-two-way-contract|date=August 7, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 7, 2025}} He was assigned to the Celtics' [[NBA G League]] team the [[Maine Celtics]] to start the season.{{Cite web |title=Maine Celtics Announce Opening Night Roster |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/roster-announced-110625 |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Maine Celtics |language=en}} On February 4, 2026, Shulga logged about two minutes of playing time for the first time in his NBA career, in a 114–93 victory over the [[2025–26 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |url=https://sport.ua/uk/news/838870-shulga-debyutuvav-v-nba-ta-dopomig-bostonu-rozgromiti-hyuston |title=Шульга дебютував в НБА та допоміг Бостону розгромити Хʼюстон |author=Олег Вахоцький |website=sport.ua |language=uk |access-date=2026-02-05 |date=2026-02-05 }} On March 15, he signed a two-year, standard contract with Celtics.{{Cite web|title=Report: Celtics to sign Max Shulga to 2-year standard contract|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/report-celtics-sign-max-shulga-033639961.html|access-date=April 19, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ===Real Madrid (2026–present)=== On July 2, 2026, Shulga joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web|title= Warriors Announce Gold and Blue Rosters for California Classic |url= https://warriors.com/news/warriors-announce-gold-and-blue-rosters-for-california-classic-20260702 |website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2026|access-date=July 2, 2026}} On August 14, 2026, Shulga signed a two-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Max Shulga swaps the NBA for Real Madrid|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/max-shulga-swaps-the-nba-for-real-madrid/|date=August 14,
